text: CHAPTER 24
speaker: Narrator

text: The First Door
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: They reached the ridge at noon on the fifth day, and the land itself was lying.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik knew the shape from his father's map—the broken line of stone that should have marked the old outpost, the shallow depression where the outer wall had collapsed, the narrow ridge that should have risen behind it like the spine of a buried animal. None of that was there.
speaker: Narrator

text: Instead they found a low mound of newer masonry half-swallowed by sand, sitting at a slight, deliberate angle to the ridge. The stones did not match. The foundations did not match. Even the way the structure had settled into the earth seemed wrong, as if the entire outpost had been built according to one set of rules and then forced to conceal another.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun noticed the discrepancy first. She dropped to her knees beside a collapsed wall and ran her fingers along the joint where newer brick met older foundation. Sand had collected in the seam, but not enough to hide the difference.
speaker: Narrator

text: This wall is lying,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik crouched beside her.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Explain.
speaker: Zik

text: It's supposed to be plumb. Straight. The foundation beneath it is aligned with the ridge, but the upper structure isn't. The entire settlement was built at an angle.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Why?
speaker: Zik

text: She looked at the wall.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: To cover what was already here.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag shifted his axe from one shoulder to the other. He had been watching the surrounding desert instead of the ruin.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We've seen enough.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu smiled the way she did when she found the weak seam in a strongbox.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We've seen nothing yet.
speaker: Enhedu

text: They worked for hours. The heat made the air shimmer above the stones. They uncovered broken pottery, ordinary foundations, the remains of a storage room, and the scattered bones of mules that had died centuries earlier. Ninsun catalogued everything she could identify. Enhedu searched the collapsed rooms for anything worth carrying. Balag did most of the heavy work and complained that everyone else had been born with useless hands.
speaker: Narrator

text: The ordinary things were almost comforting. Zik found himself wanting the ruin to remain exactly that, and the realization frightened him more than the strange parts.
speaker: Narrator

text: Every few minutes his eyes returned to the angle of the walls. His father had taught him to read construction the way other men read written language. A building told you what its builders believed about the world—what they feared, what they valued, and what they expected to happen after they were gone. This place had been built by men who expected it to remain buried.
speaker: Narrator

text: At sunset Enhedu's shovel struck stone with a different sound.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik heard it immediately.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Again.
speaker: Zik

text: She struck a second time. The hollow note came back. Balag stopped digging. Ninsun moved closer, her face tightening as she examined the exposed stone.
speaker: Narrator

text: This isn't part of the foundation.
speaker: Ninsun

text: No,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: They cleared the area carefully. The staircase began beneath the main chamber of the outpost and descended at an angle that made no architectural sense. The steps ignored the alignment of every wall above them. The upper settlement faced one direction; the staircase descended toward another.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun traced the difference with a shaking finger.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The upper settlement was built after this staircase was sealed. They knew what was down here.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag looked toward the surface.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then we go back up.
speaker: Balag

text: They built the whole place to hide the entrance,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun continued, as if she hadn't heard him.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Not around it. Over it.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik stared down into the darkness. The words from the journal returned to him, altered by everything they had learned since: the First City had never been a place of the living. It had been built to hold something down.
speaker: Narrator

text: They lit fresh torches and began the descent.
speaker: Narrator

text: The stairs ended after only twenty feet at a blank wall. There was no door, no inscription, no visible mechanism—only a seamless surface made from a material none of them recognized. It was dull and almost oily, and it did not reflect the torchlight. The flames seemed to lose their strength when held near it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun scraped away centuries of dust with her knife. Beneath it lay the spiral-drop symbol, incomplete. A section had been deliberately left out, as if whoever carved it had stopped before finishing the design.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik's left palm began to warm. He stepped closer.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik,
speaker: Balag

text: Balag said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Three measured knocks sounded from the other side of the wall.
speaker: Narrator

text: Everyone froze.
speaker: Narrator

text: The sound was not loud, which made it worse. It had been deliberate, controlled, almost polite. Three more knocks followed, patient and precise.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag's voice came out low and final.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We're leaving.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik kept his eyes on the wall.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.
